reason: The bone-lineage environment is intended to guide stem-cell descendants toward bone-forming cells, which should help build living bone.
expectation: The selected descendants will develop into bone-lineage cells.

effect: The lineage route produced bone cells, including matrix-producing osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes. I can now assemble the mature bone components.
reaction: The distinction between osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes is useful.
reason: The collagen framework and calcium phosphate are complementary structural components of the same mature bones.
expectation: The mineral will reinforce the collagen framework to form mineralized bone.

effect: The framework is now mineralised; collagen provides toughness while mineral resists compression.
reaction: The contrast between the two materials clarifies their roles.
reason: Bone cells should make the mineralised framework part of a living bone model.
expectation: The bone cells will be incorporated into the mineralised framework.

effect: Bone cells are now incorporated into the mineralised matrix, and the unfilled vessel outline identifies the remaining blood-supply detail.
reaction: The separate vessel outline makes the next step clear.
reason: Blood vessels should supply the living bone tissue and complete the arm-bone goal.
expectation: The vessels will be incorporated into the bone model to provide its blood supply.

effect: The vessels completed the living arm bones, revealing a goal to connect them into a supported, movable joint.
reaction: The cutaway usefully distinguishes the vessel from the surrounding bone tissue.
reason: The synovial membrane is described as the lining for the currently unlined fibrous joint sleeve.
expectation: The membrane will line the sleeve to form the joint capsule.

effect: The synovial membrane lined the sleeve, completing the capsule; the remaining goal is to connect the bones into a supported, movable joint.
reaction: The lining's contribution to joint fluid makes its role clearer.
reason: Articular cartilage should cover the ends of the living arm bones where they meet at the joint.
expectation: The cartilage will cap the bone ends, preparing them for the joint.

effect: The bone ends now have smooth cartilage caps that slide against one another.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: The lined capsule should surround the cartilage-covered bone ends to form the joint cavity.
expectation: The capsule will enclose the joint around the capped bone ends.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with fluid aiding their movement.
reaction: The cutaway clarifies how the lining and cartilage work together.
reason: The elbow ligaments span the joint and should provide the restraint needed for a supported, movable joint.
expectation: The ligaments will reinforce the enclosed elbow while allowing movement.

effect: The ligaments completed the movable arm skeleton, showing elbow bending alongside resistance to sideways movement. All goals are complete.
reaction: The final cutaway brings the joint's movement and restraint together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the mineralised framework was most worthwhile: the planned inset connects collagen's toughness and mineral's resistance to compression to bone structure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding bone cells was a fairly predictable assembly step, although the planned channels helped connect the cells to the later blood supply.

surprise.text: The bone-cell lineage distinguished matrix-producing osteoblasts from osteocytes embedded in the matrix, making the living tissue more than just a mineral framework.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the item descriptions and goals made the assembly sequence understandable.

continue.text: Yes, I would choose to continue: connecting material properties to the working elbow made the constructions interesting, even though the sequence was largely predictable.
